Title: LDAP Injection in LdapAdapter LDAP search filter formulation
Analysis:
The LDAP authentication settings in `LdapAdapter.cs` construct LDAP search filters using string interpolation with untrusted input `userAccountName` and `groupCN` obtained from Negotiate/Active Directory claims (which are initially provided via the client's Windows/Negotiate domain authentication). Under certain configurations, an attacker authenticated to a domain could manipulate their `sAMAccountName` (which forms part of their identity.Name) or the group names, leading to LDAP injection in the LDAP search filter `\"(&(objectClass=user)(sAMAccountName={userAccountName}))\"` or `\"(&(objectClass=group)(sAMAccountName={groupCN}))\"`. Although `identity.Name` is established via authentication, it can contain arbitrary characters depending on domain/NTLM/AD configuration, and when passed to `RetrieveClaimsAsync`, it is not sanitized or escaped for LDAP filter syntax (e.g., characters like `*`, `(`, `)`, `\`, or `\0` are not escaped), potentially modifying the LDAP query structure.
Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A user named `*` or `admin)(objectClass=user` could bypass the sAMAccountName match or inject custom search filters, altering the search behavior on the Active Directory server to fetch/map membership claims of other users.
Snippet:
var filter = $"(&(objectClass=user)(sAMAccountName={userAccountName}))"; // This is using ldap search query language, it is looking on the server for someUser
        var searchRequest = new SearchRequest(distinguishedName, filter, SearchScope.Subtree);
